findings.issue_text: `organization_context` is undefined in organization_auditlogs.py get() — evaluated unconditionally on every GET, causing NameError and 500 for all non-superuser requests

Set→zset migration is incomplete: add-buffer.lua's payload-insertion tail is unchanged and receives no timestamp/score argument, so it cannot perform a correct ZADD — if it still uses SADD it raises WRONGTYPE or creates a SET that breaks ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE/ZADD/ZSCAN; if it no longer inserts payloads, the process_spans pipeline path has no eviction at all
OptimizedCursorPaginator subclasses BasePaginator but calls CursorPaginator-only members (build_queryset, max_limit), raising AttributeError on the first optimized request

get_item_key applies math.floor/math.ceil to the raw attribute value — with order_by='-datetime' the value is a datetime object, causing TypeError on every page with results, and value_from_cursor returns a raw int that can't round-trip a DateTimeField filter

enable_advanced_features=True is passed to self.paginate(), which has an explicit signature and constructs the paginator with (queryset, key, on_results, desc) — the unexpected kwarg raises TypeError before the paginator is built

Negative-offset slicing raises ValueError: Django's QuerySet.__getitem__ rejects negative slice bounds, contradicting the comment's claim that the ORM handles negative slicing — client-controlled cursors with negative offsets cause a 500 instead of bidirectional pagination

Redirect-resolution loop limit reduced from 10000 to 1000 in add-buffer.lua — for deeper chains the loop exits with set_span_id pointing at an intermediate node, misfiling/losing spans into a set that may never be joined

max_segment_spans guard removed from _load_segment_data in buffer.py — only the byte-size cap remains, so segments of many small spans can accumulate a much larger item count before the byte cap fires and drops the entire segment

Negative-offset slicing in OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result is unsupported by Django (raises AssertionError for negative slice bounds), and the offset comes from the client-controlled cursor query param, so any request like ?optimized_pagination=true&cursor=1:-50:0 triggers a guaranteed 500; the feature cannot work as designed and should be removed

OptimizedCursorPaginator subclasses BasePaginator but calls build_queryset and _is_asc (via get_item_key), methods that only exist on CursorPaginator, so the optimized path raises AttributeError/TypeError on first invocation; additionally it is algorithmically identical to the existing DateTimePaginator keyset path and delivers none of the claimed performance benefit

Silent zpopmin eviction in add-buffer.lua discards the oldest spans once a segment's set exceeds 1000, so large segments produce silently incomplete traces with no metric or log; the replaced buffer.py._load_segment_data path at least emitted the spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded metric and an error log — add an eviction counter/metric so the data loss is observable and verify alignment with the upstream spans-per-segment limit

The same Redis keys (span-buf:s:{trace}:{span_id}) flip from set to zset (sadd→zadd, scard→zcard, sunionstore→zunionstore, sscan→zscan), causing WRONGTYPE errors on span inserts and segment flushes during rolling deploys when old and new consumers/flushers run concurrently against the same keys; add a deploy-ordering note or a type-tolerant read/migration step

Removal of the max_segment_spans guard in _load_segment_data leaves max_segment_bytes as the only in-memory bound; legacy sets written before the migration can exceed 1000 members and will be fully scanned and materialized in memory, allowing very high span counts per flush batch — the guard removal should be justified against max_segment_spans' original intent

Redirect-resolution loop bound in add-buffer.lua cut from 10,000 to 1,000 widens the known-incorrect window: trees with redirect depth >1000 will attach spans to the wrong segment; this silent behavior change at the boundary warrants a comment or metric on loop exhaustion

organization_context.member.has_global_access raises AttributeError when member is None — superusers frequently access orgs they aren't members of, causing a 500; guard with (organization_context.member and organization_context.member.has_global_access)

`organization_context` is referenced but never defined in organization_auditlogs.py and is evaluated unconditionally on every GET (not just when optimized_pagination=true), raising NameError and causing a 500 on every audit-logs request for non-superusers

OptimizedCursorPaginator is non-functional: the endpoint passes only order_by with no key, so get_item_key's getattr(item, self.key) raises TypeError on the first non-empty page, and the class copies CursorPaginator.get_result while subclassing BasePaginator, which lacks the build_queryset/key wiring that method depends on

The negative-offset branch slices queryset[start_offset:stop] with a negative start, but Django QuerySets reject negative slicing (AssertionError), so any request with optimized_pagination=true 500s; the code comment claiming the Django ORM handles negative slicing automatically is wrong

Cursors minted by the default and optimized paginator branches are not interoperable due to different key semantics, so clients alternating between the two modes get broken pagination (a response/cursor contract drift with no caller consideration)

Span buffer Redis keys change from sets to sorted sets with no key versioning, migration, or type guard, so during a rolling deploy and for pre-deploy keys still within TTL, old set commands and new zset commands both raise WRONGTYPE; process_spans fails mid-batch, arroyo retries the same batch, and the consumer stalls/backlogs until keys expire

Eviction via zpopmin silently drops the oldest buffered spans permanently with no metrics.incr or log, replacing flush-side guards that each emitted a metric plus logger.error; the effective per-segment cap becomes a hardcoded 1000 at insert time (deleting the configurable max_segment_spans check), so traces are silently truncated with no observability signal

Redirect-resolution depth bound in add-buffer.lua reduced from 10000 to 1000, so chains deeper than 1000 resolve to a mid-chain node and spans attach to non-root set keys that may never be merged upward before TTL expiry, widening the known data-loss window 10x with no compensating metric

Unrelated, externally visible API changes (new optimized_pagination query parameter on the audit-logs endpoint, modifications to the shared CursorPaginator.get_result including the max(0, offset) clamp used by every paginated endpoint) are bundled into a spans-buffer PR with no documentation, tests, or deprecation/rollout plan, making boundary review and rollback of the spans change impossible to isolate

zpopmin eviction in add-buffer.lua permanently drops the oldest spans when a set exceeds 1000 (they are never flushed), and the removed flush-time max_segment_spans guard, its spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded metric, and error log have no replacement — no metric or log was added for eviction, making this a data-loss policy change with no observability

No test coverage for the eviction behavior: nothing verifies the cap is enforced, that the oldest spans are the ones evicted, or that flush/has_root_span state stays consistent after eviction; all test updates in test_buffer.py are purely mechanical (adding the same end_timestamp_precise=1700000000.0 value for all spans), so even round-trip tests cannot detect score-ordering or eviction

Set→zset migration has no compatibility handling or test: legacy set-typed keys written by the old script (sadd/sunionstore) cause WRONGTYPE errors from the new zcard/zadd/zscan/zpopmin calls during a rolling deploy, aborting the Lua script mid-execution (span inserts fail) and breaking _load_segment_data's zscan on flush; no migration/cleanup script or integration test covers mixed old/new key formats

OptimizedCursorPaginator (~95 new lines) has zero tests and contains multiple crash bugs any basic unit test would have caught: the negative-offset branch executes queryset[start_offset:stop] with a negative start_offset, which raises Django's AssertionError (the comment claiming the ORM handles negative slicing is false); get_item_key calls math.floor on the key, which is a datetime object with order_by='-datetime' (TypeError); and the prev-cursor trim len(results) == offset + limit + extra uses the raw possibly-negative offset, so trimming silently breaks in the new branch

Audit-logs endpoint change ships with no tests and likely raises NameError on every non-superuser request: organization_context.member.has_global_access is evaluated unconditionally (only the superuser side of the or short-circuits) and organization_context does not appear in the file's imports; additionally self.paginate(..., enable_advanced_features=True) almost certainly raises TypeError since Endpoint.paginate has a fixed signature, and the superuser/global-access permission gating is completely untested

Behavioral change to shared CursorPaginator.get_result (negative-offset clamping) has no tests: non-prev cursors with negative offsets are now silently clamped to 0 while prev cursors with negative offsets still crash, affecting every cursor-paginated endpoint and converting a loud 500 into silent first-page results; sentry/utils/cursors.py now claims negative offsets are 'supported' with no validation or test pinning this down

Redirect-resolution loop limit reduced from 10000 to 1000 with no test: the removed comment explicitly documented that trees deeper than the limit 'may not be joined together correctly,' so deep parent chains now attach to a non-root set and are never joined to the segment; no test covers chain resolution at or beyond the bound

No evidence the updated tests execute the modified Lua script against real Redis: the diff converts reads/merges (scard→zcard, sunionstore→zunionstore) but shows no conversion of the command that inserts the span's payload (previously sadd) and no new ARGV for the score — if any sadd remains, inserts fail with WRONGTYPE once a zset exists; if the diff is complete and tests still pass, the tests only verify a mock/fake, so nothing demonstrates the script running end-to-end

No edge-case test for Kafka messages missing end_timestamp_precise: the direct subscript val["end_timestamp_precise"] raises KeyError on old-schema replay or malformed payloads, which in an arroyo RunTask strategy can crash-loop the partition; the test only covers the field-present happy path with no test defining expected behavior for absence

Required Span field end_timestamp_precise inserted before the defaulted is_segment_span field in buffer.py: any construction site not updated in this diff that passed is_segment_span positionally as the 6th arg will now silently bind it to end_timestamp_precise (with is_segment_span defaulting to False), causing silent data misclassification, and the PR provides no evidence that all construction sites were found

Set→zset type change with unchanged key names and no migration causes WRONGTYPE errors on legacy keys: Redis raises WRONGTYPE for zset commands (zcard/zunionstore/zadd/zscan) against keys created as sets before deploy, causing span failures for one set_timeout window after a rolling deploy; needs a key-version bump or explicit migration/compat handling

Payload-write path is never shown being converted to zadd: the script treats span-buf:s: keys as zsets but no hunk shows the incoming span's payload written with zadd (score = timestamp); if the old sadd line is unchanged every non-segment insert raises WRONGTYPE, if removed spans are silently never stored; the new ARGV (score) and matching Python call-site change are also not shown

Negative-offset slicing rests on a false premise and crashes: Django QuerySets raise ValueError for negative slice starts rather than handling them automatically as the comments claim; the enable_advanced_features branch 500s whenever a client supplies a negative-offset cursor (trivially craftable via the cursor string), and the false comments in three places will mislead future maintainers

organization_context reference is unverified and nullable: it is not defined anywhere in the shown method body, risking a NameError on every request to the endpoint; even if defined, OrganizationContext.member is optional so .member.has_global_access needs a None guard

Eviction is silent, unobservable data loss: zpopmin drops the oldest spans beyond 1000 with no metric or log, whereas the removed flush-time guard emitted metrics.incr + logger.error; eviction is also score-ordered so the segment/root span can itself be evicted while the has_root_span flag still claims it exists, producing rootless flushes

~60-line verbatim copy of CursorPaginator.get_result: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result duplicates the base implementation nearly line-for-line and has already diverged (the prev-branch compares len(results) == offset + limit + extra using offset even when start_offset was used); it should subclass CursorPaginator and override only the slicing step

Three unrelated changes bundled in one PR, one of which silently changes shared behavior: the spans zset/eviction work shares a PR with an audit-log optimized pagination feature no client uses (undocumented optimized_pagination query param) and a change to BasePaginator.get_result that alters negative-offset handling for every cursor-paginated endpoint (previously a 500, now silently clamped to page 0); these belong in separate PRs

Required field inserted mid-tuple in Span NamedTuple: end_timestamp_precise: float is added before the defaulted is_segment_span, shifting positional order so any positional construction or unpacking of Span outside the updated files misbinds or breaks silently; appending at the end would be backward-compatible

Unexplained redirect-depth limit reduction from 10000 to 1000 with the comment explaining the tradeoff deleted: trees deeper than 1000 now silently fail to join to the correct segment root; if intentional it needs a comment/metric, otherwise revert

zunionstore default AGGREGATE SUM breaks the idempotency sunionstore had: with at-least-once duplicate delivery, a payload present in both set_key and span_key/parent_key gets its score summed (2×timestamp), corrupting eviction ordering; consider AGGREGATE MIN to preserve first-seen-wins semantics

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows add-buffer.lua being updated to use ZSET operations (ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE/ZSCAN-related changes elsewhere) and Python ingestion switching to ZADD with a score (end_timestamp_precise). However, the specific claim that add-buffer.lua’s “payload-insertion tail is unchanged” and “still uses SADD / receives no timestamp” is not verifiable from the provided diff hunks because the actual insertion code path in add-buffer.lua is not shown. Therefore the asserted WRONGTYPE/incorrect-ZADD behavior is based on code not present in the diff, making the finding unconfirmable from what’s shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: OptimizedCursorPaginator subclasses BasePaginator but calls CursorPaginator-only members (build_queryset, max_limit), raising AttributeError on the first optimized request

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `OptimizedCursorPaginator` is introduced as `class OptimizedCursorPaginator(BasePaginator)` but its `get_result` calls several attributes/methods that are not defined on the class itself: `self.build_queryset(...)`, `self.max_limit`, `self.count_hits(...)`, `self.desc`, `self.key`, and `self.post_query_filter`. Unless `BasePaginator` provides these (not shown in the diff), the first request using `paginator_cls=OptimizedCursorPaginator` (added in `organization_auditlogs.py`) would raise `AttributeError` at runtime. The subclass choice (`BasePaginator` vs a cursor paginator base) makes the finding plausible and directly grounded in the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Redirect-resolution loop limit reduced from 10000 to 1000 in add-buffer.lua — for deeper chains the loop exits with set_span_id pointing at an intermediate node, misfiling/losing spans into a set that may never be joined

adjudication.rationale: In add-buffer.lua the redirect-resolution loop was changed from `for i = 0, 10000 do` to `for i = 0, 1000 do` with no additional handling when the cap is hit. The loop only breaks when `hget` returns nil or a self-loop; if the redirect chain is deeper than 1000, the loop will terminate due to the iteration limit while `set_span_id` still points to a non-terminal redirect. The script then writes `hset(main_redirect_key, span_id, set_span_id)` and unions span data into `set_key` derived from that potentially-intermediate `set_span_id`, which can leave spans partitioned under an intermediate key that may not get merged if subsequent resolutions are also capped. This is a behavior/correctness regression for deep redirect chains.

adjudication_records.issue_text: max_segment_spans guard removed from _load_segment_data in buffer.py — only the byte-size cap remains, so segments of many small spans can accumulate a much larger item count before the byte cap fires and drops the entire segment

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the span-count guard in `SpansBuffer._load_segment_data`: the block that checked `if len(payloads[key]) > self.max_segment_spans: ... del payloads[key] ...` is deleted, and only the byte-size cap remains (`if sizes[key] > self.max_segment_bytes`). While the PR adds a Redis-side cap in `add-buffer.lua` (`if span_count > 1000 then zpopmin ...`) after `zunionstore`, the Python ingestion path in `process_spans` now does a direct `zadd` of all spans in a subsegment with no corresponding count trimming. So it’s a valid review concern that large numbers of small spans could accumulate and be fully loaded/processed until the byte cap triggers, changing protective behavior; it’s not conclusively a correctness bug from the diff alone because the new Lua cap may be intended to bound cardinality in practice.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Negative-offset slicing in OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result is unsupported by Django (raises AssertionError for negative slice bounds), and the offset comes from the client-controlled cursor query param, so any request like ?optimized_pagination=true&cursor=1:-50:0 triggers a guaranteed 500; the feature cannot work as designed and should be removed

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly introduces code paths that pass a negative `start_offset` into Django queryset slicing. In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, when `enable_advanced_features` is true and `cursor.offset < 0`, it does `results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])` with `start_offset = cursor.offset` (negative). Also, even outside that branch it uses `start_offset = ... if not cursor.is_prev else offset`, so a negative `offset` with `cursor.is_prev` would also be used directly. Since `cursor.offset` is derived from the client cursor (as implied by the `Cursor` object holding `offset` and the endpoint enabling this paginator based on request params), a client can trigger negative slicing and Django QuerySet slicing with negative indices is not supported (raises), resulting in a 500. This is a real, diff-grounded broken behavior introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: OptimizedCursorPaginator subclasses BasePaginator but calls build_queryset and _is_asc (via get_item_key), methods that only exist on CursorPaginator, so the optimized path raises AttributeError/TypeError on first invocation; additionally it is algorithmically identical to the existing DateTimePaginator keyset path and delivers none of the claimed performance benefit

adjudication.rationale: In the added `OptimizedCursorPaginator(BasePaginator)` class, `get_result()` calls `self.build_queryset(cursor_value, cursor.is_prev)` and `get_item_key()` calls `self._is_asc(for_prev)`, but neither `build_queryset` nor `_is_asc` are defined on `OptimizedCursorPaginator` in this diff. Since it subclasses `BasePaginator` (not an existing cursor paginator type) and the class itself doesn’t implement those methods, the optimized code path can raise `AttributeError` when invoked from `organization_auditlogs.py` (where `paginator_cls=OptimizedCursorPaginator` is selected). The claim about being algorithmically identical to `DateTimePaginator` isn’t verifiable from the diff, but the missing-method risk is diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Silent zpopmin eviction in add-buffer.lua discards the oldest spans once a segment's set exceeds 1000, so large segments produce silently incomplete traces with no metric or log; the replaced buffer.py._load_segment_data path at least emitted the spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded metric and an error log — add an eviction counter/metric so the data loss is observable and verify alignment with the upstream spans-per-segment limit

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an unconditional cap in `src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua`: after merging spans into a sorted set, it computes `span_count` and if `span_count > 1000` it calls `redis.call("zpopmin", set_key, span_count - 1000)`, which silently discards entries (oldest by score). There is no metric/log emitted in the Lua script. At the same time, `src/sentry/spans/buffer.py` removes the prior span-count guard/observability in `_load_segment_data` (the `max_segment_spans` check that incremented `spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded` and logged an error was deleted). Together, this introduces silent trace truncation/data loss for large segments with no visibility, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The same Redis keys (span-buf:s:{trace}:{span_id}) flip from set to zset (sadd→zadd, scard→zcard, sunionstore→zunionstore, sscan→zscan), causing WRONGTYPE errors on span inserts and segment flushes during rolling deploys when old and new consumers/flushers run concurrently against the same keys; add a deploy-ordering note or a type-tolerant read/migration step

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the Redis data structure for the existing key pattern `span-buf:s:{...}:{...}` from a Set to a Sorted Set: `SpansBuffer.process_spans` switches `sadd` -> `zadd` (buffer.py:194-199), `_load_segment_data` switches `sscan` -> `zscan` (buffer.py:431-446), and the Lua script switches `scard/sunionstore` -> `zcard/zunionstore` and adds `zpopmin` trimming (add-buffer.lua:45-71). The key name (`span-buf:s:{project_and_trace}:{span_id/parent_span_id}`) is unchanged, so during a rolling deploy where old and new code run concurrently, one side may create/use the key as a Set while the other uses ZSET commands, which in Redis will raise WRONGTYPE errors on inserts/unions/scans. The diff does not include any type-tolerant migration/read path or deploy-ordering guard, so the finding describes a real, diff-grounded correctness/deploy bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removal of the max_segment_spans guard in _load_segment_data leaves max_segment_bytes as the only in-memory bound; legacy sets written before the migration can exceed 1000 members and will be fully scanned and materialized in memory, allowing very high span counts per flush batch — the guard removal should be justified against max_segment_spans' original intent

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the `max_segment_spans` in-memory guard in `SpansBuffer._load_segment_data`: previously it checked `len(payloads[key]) > self.max_segment_spans` and aborted the segment; now it only enforces `self.max_segment_bytes` while accumulating results from `p.zscan(...)` and unconditionally `payloads[key].extend(...)`. While the Lua changes add a 1000-member cap for newly written data (`zpopmin` when `span_count > 1000`), nothing in this diff demonstrates a backfill/migration for pre-existing Redis keys, so a reviewer could reasonably ask for justification of removing the span-count guard given its original intent (protecting against high span counts per segment/flush) even if bytes still bounds memory.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Redirect-resolution loop bound in add-buffer.lua cut from 10,000 to 1,000 widens the known-incorrect window: trees with redirect depth >1000 will attach spans to the wrong segment; this silent behavior change at the boundary warrants a comment or metric on loop exhaustion

adjudication.rationale: The diff reduces the redirect-resolution loop in `add-buffer.lua` from `for i = 0, 10000 do` (with an explicit comment about incorrect joining beyond that depth) to `for i = 0, 1000 do` and removes the explanatory comment. There is still no explicit handling/metric/logging when the loop exhausts without hitting the break condition, so if redirect chains exceed 1000, the script will silently proceed with whatever `set_span_id` it has at that point. The exact frequency/impact of >1000 depth isn’t provable from the diff alone, but the change clearly tightens the bound without any guardrails.

adjudication_records.issue_text: organization_context.member.has_global_access raises AttributeError when member is None — superusers frequently access orgs they aren't members of, causing a 500; guard with (organization_context.member and organization_context.member.has_global_access)

adjudication.rationale: In the new code, `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` short-circuits: for superusers, `organization_context.member.has_global_access` is not evaluated, so the stated "superusers frequently access orgs they aren't members of" path would not raise `AttributeError`. Whether `organization_context.member` can be `None` for non-superusers cannot be verified from this diff alone (permissions/context creation not shown).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `organization_context` is referenced but never defined in organization_auditlogs.py and is evaluated unconditionally on every GET (not just when optimized_pagination=true), raising NameError and causing a 500 on every audit-logs request for non-superusers

adjudication.rationale: In `organization_auditlogs.py`, the new logic computes `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` before the `if use_optimized and enable_advanced:` branch. In the shown diff hunk, `organization_context` is not defined anywhere in the function/file context, so this reference would raise `NameError` regardless of `optimized_pagination`, breaking the endpoint (500) for non-superusers as well.

adjudication_records.issue_text: OptimizedCursorPaginator is non-functional: the endpoint passes only order_by with no key, so get_item_key's getattr(item, self.key) raises TypeError on the first non-empty page, and the class copies CursorPaginator.get_result while subclassing BasePaginator, which lacks the build_queryset/key wiring that method depends on

adjudication.rationale: In `organization_auditlogs.py`, the endpoint switches to `paginator_cls=OptimizedCursorPaginator` but only supplies `order_by="-datetime"` (no `key` argument). The new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` implementation calls `get_item_key()` which does `getattr(item, self.key)`, and `get_result()` calls `self.build_queryset(...)`; neither `self.key` nor `build_queryset` are defined anywhere in `OptimizedCursorPaginator` itself. From the diff alone, this makes the new code path very likely to error at runtime (TypeError/AttributeError) on the first non-empty page when `optimized_pagination=true` is used.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The negative-offset branch slices queryset[start_offset:stop] with a negative start, but Django QuerySets reject negative slicing (AssertionError), so any request with optimized_pagination=true 500s; the code comment claiming the Django ORM handles negative slicing automatically is wrong

adjudication.rationale: The new `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` explicitly allows `start_offset = cursor.offset` when `enable_advanced_features` and `cursor.offset < 0`, then slices `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative start. Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative indices (it asserts non-negative start/stop), so a request that supplies a cursor with a negative `offset` would raise and likely 500. The comment claiming the ORM handles negative slicing automatically is therefore incorrect. (The finding overstates impact: it’s not *any* `optimized_pagination=true` request, only those with a negative offset in the cursor.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cursors minted by the default and optimized paginator branches are not interoperable due to different key semantics, so clients alternating between the two modes get broken pagination (a response/cursor contract drift with no caller consideration)

adjudication.rationale: The endpoint now conditionally switches `paginator_cls` between `DateTimePaginator` and the new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` based on `optimized_pagination=true` and an admin check. Since the paginator implementation is part of the cursor contract, this conditional makes it plausible that cursors produced in one mode may not be valid/meaningful in the other if a client drops/adds the flag between requests. The diff does not prove the two paginator cursor formats/keys are different, but it introduces an API mode split without any visible compatibility/translation layer or caller guidance.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Span buffer Redis keys change from sets to sorted sets with no key versioning, migration, or type guard, so during a rolling deploy and for pre-deploy keys still within TTL, old set commands and new zset commands both raise WRONGTYPE; process_spans fails mid-batch, arroyo retries the same batch, and the consumer stalls/backlogs until keys expire

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the Redis data structure for the same key pattern `span-buf:s:{...}:...` from a Set to a Sorted Set: `SpansBuffer.process_spans` switches `SADD` to `ZADD` (buffer.py), `_load_segment_data` switches `SSCAN` to `ZSCAN`, and the Lua script switches `SCARD/SUNIONSTORE` to `ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE` and adds `ZPOPMIN` trimming (add-buffer.lua). There is no key versioning/prefix change, migration path, or runtime type-check/guard shown. During a rolling deploy, existing keys within TTL created by old code (Set) will cause new code/Lua to issue Z* commands against a Set (or vice versa), which Redis will reject with WRONGTYPE, breaking processing until the old keys expire.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Eviction via zpopmin silently drops the oldest buffered spans permanently with no metrics.incr or log, replacing flush-side guards that each emitted a metric plus logger.error; the effective per-segment cap becomes a hardcoded 1000 at insert time (deleting the configurable max_segment_spans check), so traces are silently truncated with no observability signal

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces hard eviction in `add-buffer.lua` by capping each segment ZSET to 1000 entries via `zpopmin(set_key, span_count - 1000)` with no `metrics.incr`/logging anywhere in that code path. At the same time, `SpansBuffer._load_segment_data` removes the previous `max_segment_spans` guard that emitted `metrics.incr("...segment_span_count_exceeded")` and `logger.error(...)` and would drop the segment when too many spans were present. Net effect is silent truncation (dropping oldest spans) and the effective cap becomes a hardcoded 1000 at write/merge time rather than the configurable `max_segment_spans`, with no observability signal—this is verifiable directly from the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Redirect-resolution depth bound in add-buffer.lua reduced from 10000 to 1000, so chains deeper than 1000 resolve to a mid-chain node and spans attach to non-root set keys that may never be merged upward before TTL expiry, widening the known data-loss window 10x with no compensating metric

adjudication.rationale: The diff does reduce the redirect-resolution loop in `add-buffer.lua` from `for i = 0, 10000 do` to `for i = 0, 1000 do` with no new fallback when the loop exhausts. If the redirect chain is deeper than 1000, the script will stop early and proceed using a mid-chain `set_span_id`, which can change which `set_key` spans are unioned into. However, the finding’s stronger claims ("may never be merged upward before TTL expiry", "widening ... data-loss window 10x") are not directly verifiable from this diff alone (TTL/merge guarantees and prior data-loss behavior aren’t shown). This is a concrete edge-case/robustness regression but not a provable defect from the patch by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unrelated, externally visible API changes (new optimized_pagination query parameter on the audit-logs endpoint, modifications to the shared CursorPaginator.get_result including the max(0, offset) clamp used by every paginated endpoint) are bundled into a spans-buffer PR with no documentation, tests, or deprecation/rollout plan, making boundary review and rollback of the spans change impossible to isolate

adjudication.rationale: The diff includes externally visible and shared pagination changes unrelated to spans buffering: (1) `organization_auditlogs.py` adds a new `optimized_pagination=true` query parameter and conditional use of `OptimizedCursorPaginator` with `enable_advanced_features=True`; (2) `src/sentry/api/paginator.py` changes shared `get_result` slicing behavior via `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`, affecting all endpoints using that paginator; and (3) it introduces a new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` class. These are bundled alongside the spans-buffer Redis set→sorted-set changes, and the diff shows no accompanying tests or rollout/deprecation scaffolding for the API/pagination behavior changes, making the scope/rollback harder to isolate. This is a concrete scope/architecture/reviewability issue rather than a provable functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: zpopmin eviction in add-buffer.lua permanently drops the oldest spans when a set exceeds 1000 (they are never flushed), and the removed flush-time max_segment_spans guard, its spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded metric, and error log have no replacement — no metric or log was added for eviction, making this a data-loss policy change with no observability

adjudication.rationale: In `add-buffer.lua`, after merging into the sorted set (`zunionstore` / `zcard`), the script enforces a hard cap: `if span_count > 1000 then redis.call("zpopmin", set_key, span_count - 1000) end`. This removes the lowest-score (oldest by `end_timestamp_precise`) spans from the buffer key, and because they are deleted from Redis, they cannot be flushed later (permanent data drop from the buffer). In `spans/buffer.py`, the previous `max_segment_spans` overflow guard and its observability (`spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded` metric + error log) were removed when switching from `sscan` to `zscan`, and no new metric/log was added for the new eviction behavior in the Lua script. The diff therefore introduces a silent data-loss policy change with reduced observability, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test coverage for the eviction behavior: nothing verifies the cap is enforced, that the oldest spans are the ones evicted, or that flush/has_root_span state stays consistent after eviction; all test updates in test_buffer.py are purely mechanical (adding the same end_timestamp_precise=1700000000.0 value for all spans), so even round-trip tests cannot detect score-ordering or eviction

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new nontrivial eviction and ordering behavior in `add-buffer.lua`: it switches span storage from sets to sorted sets (`zadd`, `zscan`) and enforces a hard cap via `if span_count > 1000 then redis.call("zpopmin", set_key, span_count - 1000) end`, which implies oldest-by-score eviction (score = `end_timestamp_precise` as written in `buffer.py` via `p.zadd(set_key, {span.payload: span.end_timestamp_precise ...})`). The updated tests (`tests/sentry/spans/test_buffer.py`, flusher/consumer tests) only mechanically add `end_timestamp_precise=1700000000.0` everywhere and do not assert the 1000-cap, which members are evicted, or that subsequent flush/has_root_span behavior remains consistent after eviction. This is a specific, diff-grounded missing coverage concern rather than a demonstrable runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Set→zset migration has no compatibility handling or test: legacy set-typed keys written by the old script (sadd/sunionstore) cause WRONGTYPE errors from the new zcard/zadd/zscan/zpopmin calls during a rolling deploy, aborting the Lua script mid-execution (span inserts fail) and breaking _load_segment_data's zscan on flush; no migration/cleanup script or integration test covers mixed old/new key formats

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes span buffer Redis storage from SETs to ZSETs: Lua now uses `zcard`, `zunionstore`, `zpopmin` on `span_key`/`parent_key`/`set_key` (add-buffer.lua), and Python now writes with `zadd` and reads with `zscan` (buffer.py). There is no compatibility path for pre-existing keys that were previously created/maintained as SETs via `sadd`/`sunionstore`/`sscan`. In Redis, issuing ZSET commands (e.g. `ZCARD`, `ZSCAN`, `ZUNIONSTORE`) against a SET key returns `WRONGTYPE`, which would abort the Lua script mid-execution and break `_load_segment_data`’s `zscan` when encountering legacy keys during a rolling deploy. The diff also contains no migration/cleanup logic or tests covering mixed key types.

adjudication_records.issue_text: OptimizedCursorPaginator (~95 new lines) has zero tests and contains multiple crash bugs any basic unit test would have caught: the negative-offset branch executes queryset[start_offset:stop] with a negative start_offset, which raises Django's AssertionError (the comment claiming the ORM handles negative slicing is false); get_item_key calls math.floor on the key, which is a datetime object with order_by='-datetime' (TypeError); and the prev-cursor trim len(results) == offset + limit + extra uses the raw possibly-negative offset, so trimming silently breaks in the new branch

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` and wires it into `organization_auditlogs.get()` with `order_by="-datetime"`. In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key`, it does `math.floor(value)`/`math.ceil(value)` on `value = getattr(item, self.key)`. With audit logs ordered by `datetime`, that value is a datetime, so this will raise a `TypeError` when generating cursors/keys. Additionally, the new "advanced" negative-offset path explicitly slices `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with `start_offset = cursor.offset` when `cursor.offset < 0`; Django `QuerySet` slicing does not support negative slice bounds, so this is a crash path. The prev-cursor trimming logic also compares `len(results)` to `offset + limit + extra` using the raw (possibly negative) `offset`, which will break trimming behavior in that branch. No tests are added for this new paginator/branch in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Audit-logs endpoint change ships with no tests and likely raises NameError on every non-superuser request: organization_context.member.has_global_access is evaluated unconditionally (only the superuser side of the or short-circuits) and organization_context does not appear in the file's imports; additionally self.paginate(..., enable_advanced_features=True) almost certainly raises TypeError since Endpoint.paginate has a fixed signature, and the superuser/global-access permission gating is completely untested

adjudication.rationale: In `organization_auditlogs.py`, the new line `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` references `organization_context`, but the diff shows no definition/import of `organization_context` in this file or method. Due to Python `or` short-circuiting, this will raise `NameError` for any non-superuser request when it evaluates the second operand. The finding’s broader point about missing tests is secondary, but the undefined name is a concrete runtime defect introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Behavioral change to shared CursorPaginator.get_result (negative-offset clamping) has no tests: non-prev cursors with negative offsets are now silently clamped to 0 while prev cursors with negative offsets still crash, affecting every cursor-paginated endpoint and converting a loud 500 into silent first-page results; sentry/utils/cursors.py now claims negative offsets are 'supported' with no validation or test pinning this down

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes shared pagination slicing behavior in `src/sentry/api/paginator.py` to clamp `offset` to 0 for non-`is_prev` cursors (`start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`), which will turn previously erroring negative offsets into “first page” results. At the same time, `is_prev` keeps using the raw (potentially negative) `offset`, which can still raise on negative queryset slicing. `src/sentry/utils/cursors.py` also adds commentary implying negative offsets are supported without adding any validation or tests. No tests in the diff cover these negative-offset behaviors, so the concern is specific and diff-grounded, but not unequivocally a defect without the intended contract.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Redirect-resolution loop limit reduced from 10000 to 1000 with no test: the removed comment explicitly documented that trees deeper than the limit 'may not be joined together correctly,' so deep parent chains now attach to a non-root set and are never joined to the segment; no test covers chain resolution at or beyond the bound

adjudication.rationale: The diff does reduce the redirect-resolution loop in `src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua` from `for i = 0, 10000 do` (with an explicit comment warning that deeper trees may not join correctly) to `for i = 0, 1000 do` and removes that warning. This is a concrete behavior change that increases the chance of hitting the bound and leaving `set_span_id` unresolved if the redirect chain exceeds 1000. The diff does not add/modify any tests to exercise redirect resolution at/near this bound. However, the claim that such spans are "never joined" cannot be fully proven from the diff alone, so this is best treated as an untested edge-case/regression risk rather than a definitively verified defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No evidence the updated tests execute the modified Lua script against real Redis: the diff converts reads/merges (scard→zcard, sunionstore→zunionstore) but shows no conversion of the command that inserts the span's payload (previously sadd) and no new ARGV for the score — if any sadd remains, inserts fail with WRONGTYPE once a zset exists; if the diff is complete and tests still pass, the tests only verify a mock/fake, so nothing demonstrates the script running end-to-end

adjudication.rationale: The diff *does* convert the insertion path from `sadd` to `zadd` in `src/sentry/spans/buffer.py` (`p.zadd(set_key, {span.payload: span.end_timestamp_precise ...})`) and adds the required `end_timestamp_precise` field through the consumer and tests. The Lua script (`add-buffer.lua`) shown still doesn’t insert payloads at all (it only merges/redirects keys), so the claim that a leftover `sadd` would fail with WRONGTYPE is not supported by what’s in this diff. The assertion that tests must be using a mock/fake Redis is also speculative and not verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No edge-case test for Kafka messages missing end_timestamp_precise: the direct subscript val["end_timestamp_precise"] raises KeyError on old-schema replay or malformed payloads, which in an arroyo RunTask strategy can crash-loop the partition; the test only covers the field-present happy path with no test defining expected behavior for absence

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/factory.py`, the change makes `end_timestamp_precise` a required field via direct subscript (`end_timestamp_precise=val["end_timestamp_precise"]`). The updated tests only add the field in happy-path payloads (e.g. `tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py`) and do not cover/define behavior when the field is absent. While absence may be impossible if the Kafka schema guarantees it, the diff does introduce a new required key and no edge-case test documents handling of missing/old payloads.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Required Span field end_timestamp_precise inserted before the defaulted is_segment_span field in buffer.py: any construction site not updated in this diff that passed is_segment_span positionally as the 6th arg will now silently bind it to end_timestamp_precise (with is_segment_span defaulting to False), causing silent data misclassification, and the PR provides no evidence that all construction sites were found

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new required field `end_timestamp_precise` to `Span(NamedTuple)` in `src/sentry/spans/buffer.py` and places it before the defaulted `is_segment_span` field. This creates a real risk that any existing *positional* `Span(...)` construction elsewhere in the codebase (not shown in this diff) that previously passed `is_segment_span` as the 6th argument would now bind that value to `end_timestamp_precise` and silently change `is_segment_span` to its default. In this diff, the shown call sites use keyword arguments and were updated, but the finding’s claim about other call sites cannot be verified from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Set→zset type change with unchanged key names and no migration causes WRONGTYPE errors on legacy keys: Redis raises WRONGTYPE for zset commands (zcard/zunionstore/zadd/zscan) against keys created as sets before deploy, causing span failures for one set_timeout window after a rolling deploy; needs a key-version bump or explicit migration/compat handling

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes Redis data structures for the same key patterns from sets to sorted sets without any compatibility/migration layer. In `spans/buffer.py`, `process_spans` now writes `span-buf:s:{...}:{...}` via `ZADD` instead of `SADD`, and `_load_segment_data` now reads via `ZSCAN` instead of `SSCAN`. In `scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua`, the same keys are manipulated with `ZCARD`/`ZUNIONSTORE`/`ZPOPMIN` instead of `SCARD`/`SUNIONSTORE`. If a rolling deploy leaves existing keys of type SET (created by the old code) alive (they’re only expired via `expire`), the new code will issue zset commands against SET keys, which Redis will reject with `WRONGTYPE`, breaking span buffering/flush until those legacy keys expire. No key-version bump or fallback logic is shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Payload-write path is never shown being converted to zadd: the script treats span-buf:s: keys as zsets but no hunk shows the incoming span's payload written with zadd (score = timestamp); if the old sadd line is unchanged every non-segment insert raises WRONGTYPE, if removed spans are silently never stored; the new ARGV (score) and matching Python call-site change are also not shown

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly shows the payload-write path being converted from `sadd` to `zadd` with a score: in `src/sentry/spans/buffer.py` `process_spans` changes `p.sadd(set_key, *[span.payload ...])` to `p.zadd(set_key, {span.payload: span.end_timestamp_precise ...})`. The `Span` tuple gains `end_timestamp_precise`, the Kafka consumer populates it from the parsed payload, and the Lua script is updated to use `zcard/zunionstore/zscan` semantics. So the claim that the conversion is “never shown” and that an ARGV/score call-site change is missing is contradicted by the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: OptimizedCursorPaginator is unusable as wired: build_queryset is defined on CursorPaginator not BasePaginator so self.build_queryset(...) fails, and the endpoint passes no key so get_item_key executes getattr(item, None) → TypeError; the optimized path 500s on first invocation and should subclass CursorPaginator with key='datetime'

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `OptimizedCursorPaginator` is introduced as `class OptimizedCursorPaginator(BasePaginator)` and its `get_result` calls `self.build_queryset(cursor_value, cursor.is_prev)`, but this new class itself does not define `build_queryset` and there is no indication in the diff that `BasePaginator` gained it—so this will raise `AttributeError` if `BasePaginator` lacks that method. Separately, `get_item_key` does `getattr(item, self.key)` but `OptimizedCursorPaginator` does not define a `key` (e.g. `key = "datetime"`) and the endpoint wires it via `self.paginate(... paginator_cls=OptimizedCursorPaginator, order_by="-datetime", ...)` without passing a `key`, so `self.key` is likely `None`, making `getattr(item, None)` invalid and causing a 500 on the optimized path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Negative-offset slicing rests on a false premise and crashes: Django QuerySets raise ValueError for negative slice starts rather than handling them automatically as the comments claim; the enable_advanced_features branch 500s whenever a client supplies a negative-offset cursor (trivially craftable via the cursor string), and the false comments in three places will mislead future maintainers

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces/endorses negative start offsets for QuerySet slicing, but Django QuerySets do not support negative slice indices. In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, the `enable_advanced_features` branch explicitly does `results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])` with `start_offset = cursor.offset` when `cursor.offset < 0` (new code in `src/sentry/api/paginator.py`), and the earlier paginator change also allows a negative `offset` through when `cursor.is_prev` (`start_offset = ... if not cursor.is_prev else offset`). If a client supplies/crafts a cursor with a negative `offset`, this can raise at slice time and 500 the endpoint. The added comments in `paginator.py` and `utils/cursors.py` claim negative offsets are "safe"/"handled" by the ORM, which is incorrect and risks misleading maintainers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: organization_context reference is unverified and nullable: it is not defined anywhere in the shown method body, risking a NameError on every request to the endpoint; even if defined, OrganizationContext.member is optional so .member.has_global_access needs a None guard
matched_golden_ids: Accessing .has_global_access on organization_context.member can raise an AttributeError when organization_context is None, particularly for non-superuser non-member users.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that `organization_context` may be null/undefined and that dereferencing `.member.has_global_access` needs a None guard. This covers the golden issue (AttributeError when `organization_context` is None), even though it additionally mentions a possible NameError.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Eviction is silent, unobservable data loss: zpopmin drops the oldest spans beyond 1000 with no metric or log, whereas the removed flush-time guard emitted metrics.incr + logger.error; eviction is also score-ordered so the segment/root span can itself be evicted while the has_root_span flag still claims it exists, producing rootless flushes

adjudication.rationale: In `add-buffer.lua` the new cap logic unconditionally evicts spans via `zpopmin` when `span_count > 1000` with no metric/log (`if span_count > 1000 then redis.call("zpopmin", ...) end`). At the same time, the previous observable guard in `SpansBuffer._load_segment_data` that emitted `metrics.incr(...)` + `logger.error(...)` and skipped oversized segments was removed entirely (the whole `if len(payloads[key]) > self.max_segment_spans: ...` block is deleted). This introduces silent, hard-to-observe span loss. Additionally, eviction is score-ordered by `end_timestamp_precise` (Python now does `zadd(set_key, {span.payload: span.end_timestamp_precise ...})`), so the oldest-by-score spans are dropped; nothing in the Lua cap protects the root/segment span from being among those evicted. Yet `has_root_span` is derived from a separate Redis key (`span-buf:hrs:%s`) that is not coupled to membership in the zset, so it can claim a root exists even if that root payload was evicted, leading to potential rootless flush behavior as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The 1000-span bound is enforced on only one of two write paths: process_spans zadds segment spans into set_key directly with no eviction and the flusher's max_segment_spans guard was deleted, so segment-span sets remain unbounded and the memory-bounding motivation of the PR isn't achieved

adjudication.rationale: Diff adds a 1000-element cap only in `scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua` via `zcard`/`zpopmin`, but `SpansBuffer.process_spans` now writes directly to the same `span-buf:s:{...}` keys with `p.zadd(...)` and no trimming/eviction. Additionally, `_load_segment_data` removed the `max_segment_spans` guard that previously prevented overly large segments from being processed. From the diff alone, this means one write path remains unbounded and the earlier span-count protection was deleted, so Redis segment sorted-sets can grow without a 1000-span bound.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ~60-line verbatim copy of CursorPaginator.get_result: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result duplicates the base implementation nearly line-for-line and has already diverged (the prev-branch compares len(results) == offset + limit + extra using offset even when start_offset was used); it should subclass CursorPaginator and override only the slicing step

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` in `src/sentry/api/paginator.py` that largely reimplements the existing cursor pagination flow (cursor normalization, queryset build, hit counting, offset/extra handling, prev trimming/reversal, `build_cursor`, post-query filter). This is a concrete maintainability/architecture issue introduced by the change: the duplicated logic is long and easy to drift from the established paginator behavior. While the finding’s specific example about `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` vs `start_offset` isn’t clearly verifiable as a correctness bug from the shown code (that check is inside the `cursor.is_prev` branch where `start_offset` is set to `offset`), the broader point about near-verbatim duplication and divergence risk is grounded in the diff and actionable (prefer subclassing/overriding just the slicing behavior).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Three unrelated changes bundled in one PR, one of which silently changes shared behavior: the spans zset/eviction work shares a PR with an audit-log optimized pagination feature no client uses (undocumented optimized_pagination query param) and a change to BasePaginator.get_result that alters negative-offset handling for every cursor-paginated endpoint (previously a 500, now silently clamped to page 0); these belong in separate PRs

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly bundles multiple unrelated features: (1) audit log endpoint adds an undocumented `optimized_pagination=true` query param and conditionally uses a new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` (organization_auditlogs.py), (2) `BasePaginator.get_result` changes slicing to clamp negative offsets to 0 when not `cursor.is_prev` (paginator.py), altering shared pagination behavior across endpoints, and (3) spans buffer storage changes from sets to zsets with eviction logic (Lua + buffer.py). The “no client uses” part isn’t verifiable from the diff, but the scope/architecture concern and the global behavior change are diff-grounded and actionable, without necessarily being a defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Required field inserted mid-tuple in Span NamedTuple: end_timestamp_precise: float is added before the defaulted is_segment_span, shifting positional order so any positional construction or unpacking of Span outside the updated files misbinds or breaks silently; appending at the end would be backward-compatible

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `Span(NamedTuple)` field order by inserting a new required field `end_timestamp_precise: float` before the previously-last defaulted field `is_segment_span: bool = False` (src/sentry/spans/buffer.py). This is a backward-incompatible API change for any existing *positional* `Span(...)` construction or tuple-unpacking elsewhere: old 6-arg calls would now bind the 6th arg to `end_timestamp_precise` and silently leave `is_segment_span` at its default. In the diff, updated call sites use keyword args, so no immediate break is shown here, but the compatibility risk is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unexplained redirect-depth limit reduction from 10000 to 1000 with the comment explaining the tradeoff deleted: trees deeper than 1000 now silently fail to join to the correct segment root; if intentional it needs a comment/metric, otherwise revert

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua`, the redirect-follow loop limit is reduced from `for i = 0, 10000 do  -- ... depth 10k may not be joined ...` to `for i = 0, 1000 do` and the explanatory comment is removed. This is a concrete behavior/edge-case change: chains deeper than 1000 will stop early and potentially not resolve to the intended `set_span_id`, but the diff doesn’t show whether such depths are possible in practice. The finding’s request for justification (comment/metric) is grounded in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: zunionstore default AGGREGATE SUM breaks the idempotency sunionstore had: with at-least-once duplicate delivery, a payload present in both set_key and span_key/parent_key gets its score summed (2×timestamp), corrupting eviction ordering; consider AGGREGATE MIN to preserve first-seen-wins semantics

adjudication.rationale:
In `src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua`, the diff replaces `sunionstore` with `zunionstore`:
- `span_count = redis.call("zunionstore", set_key, 2, set_key, span_key)` (and similarly with `parent_key`).
Redis `ZUNIONSTORE` defaults to `AGGREGATE SUM`. If the same `span.payload` member exists in both `set_key` and `span_key`/`parent_key` (plausible with at-least-once delivery or repeated merges), the resulting score becomes the sum (e.g., `2 * end_timestamp_precise`) instead of preserving the intended timestamp score. Since the code later evicts using `zpopmin` based on score (`if span_count > 1000 then ... zpopmin ...`), summing scores can corrupt ordering/eviction behavior. The finding’s suggestion to specify a non-summing aggregate (e.g., `AGGREGATE MIN`) is directly grounded in this change.

adjudication.rationale: In `organization_auditlogs.py`, the new line `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` is evaluated unconditionally (before the `if use_optimized and enable_advanced` branch). In the shown diff hunk there is no definition of `organization_context`, so if it is not defined earlier in the method/file this would raise `NameError` on every GET and 500 the endpoint. The additional concern about `.member` possibly being `None` is plausible but not verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add-buffer.lua/buffer.py switch the same Redis keys (`span-buf:s:...`) from sets (sadd/sscan) to zsets (zcard/zunionstore/zpopmin/zscan) with no migration, version marker, dual-write, or type-check, causing WRONGTYPE failures during rolling deploy (old processes write sets, new code errors entire span batches in the consumer and fails _load_segment_data for legacy keys) and the mirror problem on rollback (scard/sscan on zsets), persisting until old keys expire

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the Redis data type for the same key pattern `span-buf:s:{...}:<id>` from SETs to ZSETs without any compatibility layer. In `buffer.py`, `process_spans` switches from `sadd` to `zadd` for `set_key`, and `_load_segment_data` switches from `sscan` to `zscan`. In `add-buffer.lua`, the same keys are now manipulated with `zcard`/`zunionstore`/`zpopmin` instead of `scard`/`sunionstore`. Redis will raise `WRONGTYPE` if a key exists with the other type (e.g., old code created a SET, new code calls `zcard`/`zscan`, or rollback calls `scard`/`sscan` on a ZSET). The diff shows no migration, versioned key, type-check, or dual-read/write to prevent rolling-deploy/rollback failures; the mismatch would persist until key expiry.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add-buffer.lua (~lines 56-63) silently evicts the oldest spans via zpopmin with a hardcoded per-segment cap of 1000, causing silent partial-trace data loss under sustained insertion (TTL keeps refreshing so older spans are never flushed); the removed Python-side guard (segment_span_count_exceeded metric, error log, atomic skip-whole-segment behavior) is not replaced and Lua cannot emit metrics, the hardcoded 1000 is likely stricter than the removed max_segment_spans, and no test covers the eviction path

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add a hard per-segment cap in `add-buffer.lua`: after computing `span_count`, it calls `zpopmin(set_key, span_count - 1000)` when `span_count > 1000`, which will silently remove the lowest-score entries (with scores set from `end_timestamp_precise` via `zadd` in `spans/buffer.py`). In parallel, the Python-side span-count safeguard in `_load_segment_data` that logged/metric’d and skipped whole segments when `len(payloads[key]) > self.max_segment_spans` is removed, and nothing in the Lua path emits a metric or log. The cap value is hardcoded to 1000 in Lua and no tests in the diff cover the eviction behavior. However, because this eviction appears intentionally introduced as a memory/size control mechanism (not an accidental breakage), it’s better classified as a significant review concern (changed semantics/observability/test coverage) rather than a provable defect.
